items.summary: Binance said it is discussing a licensed business pathway with the Securities Commission and Bank Negara Malaysia, according to a spokesperson citing Bloomberg. The exchange seeks to re-enter a market where regulators blocked its website and applications since July 2021. Binance reported this week that a security breach may have cost as much as US$6.3 billion (S$8 billion), prompting lawmaker Lim Guan Eng to request an investigation into possible ringgit transactions on its platform.
items.title: Binance in talks for Malaysia licence after five-year absence

items.summary: A security researcher named Mark Blah released a proof-of-concept exploit for CVE-2026-58882, an Android vulnerability dubbed 'SMS of Death.' The zero-click denial-of-service flaw lets attackers crash phones or disrupt calls—including emergency calls—by sending one crafted text message. Google reportedly patched it in its October 2026 updates for Android 14 through 17, but older Android 12 and 13 devices remain vulnerable.
items.title: Android SMS of Death exploit crashes unpatched phones remotely

items.summary: Meta’s agentic AI tool Muse has drawn attention on recent corporate earnings calls, though executives across roughly 50 companies in sectors including travel, internet providers, food and self-storage largely shrugged off immediate disruption. Some described agent-driven bookings as “insignificant” or “quite low,” while others said they expect to benefit from widespread adoption. Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg reported that more than 10 million people in the US and Canada had activated Muse, with over 25 percent using it for shopping. Meanwhile, companies like Chipotle are adjusting their websites after agents struggled with loyalty discounts, and Bank of America cautioned customers about sharing login information with AI assistants.
items.title: Meta’s AI Shopping Tool Faces Skepticism From Businesses

items.summary: Reddit announced it will gradually become a logged-in service, limiting full content access for visitors without accounts in selected markets outside the United States. Co-founder Steve Huffman said the change aims to improve personalization and combat scraping, since most unauthorized data access occurs through logged-out pages. Logged users may opt out of personalized advertising; real-name requirements are not needed.
items.title: Reddit to lock content behind logins to fight scrapers

items.summary: This Past Forward column traces how early electric cars were positioned for women drivers, using a mercury-arc rectifier charger and Fannie Goodnow's 1908 Bailey Victoria Phaeton as examples. At the turn of the century, U.S. carmakers grew from about 50 in 1898 to five times that number by 1901, when production reached 7,000 vehicles; by 1910 it had hit 181,000. Electric cars competed with steam and gasoline models, but were marketed as easy to start and clean-running. General Electric ran ads showing women plugging in their cars. Goodnow's charger now sits at Heritage Museums & Gardens in Sandwich, Mass., while her car is lost. S.R. Bailey & Co., which built the Victoria Phaeton after entering electric vehicles in 1906 amid a collapsing carriage business, produced about 500 to 600 such cars before selling its factory in 1915.
items.title: Early Electric Cars Marketed Toward Women Drivers

items.summary: The Environmental Protection Agency updated its webpage this week, setting a final expiration date of December 31, 2026 for its online web archive. Gretchen Gehrke of the Environmental Data and Governance Initiative said the archive holds irreplaceable information dating back at least 20 years that would be lost if decommissioned. The agency has considered closing it before; after public backlash in 2023, it delayed retirement to July 2023 and later relabeled the move as a “retiring.” Lauren Harper of the Freedom of Press Foundation warned the closure could erode trust amid low confidence in government. The EPA did not respond to a request for comment.
items.title: EPA Sets December 2026 Deadline to Shut Down Its Web Archive

items.summary: The government of Senegal is pursuing an ambitious energy diversification strategy under its Vision 2050 plan, aiming to reduce reliance on expensive heavy fuel oil by transitioning to natural gas and renewable energy. According to government figures, oil-based fuels accounted for approximately 72.5 per cent of national power production in 2024. The country also faces high electricity generation costs estimated between 34 and 38 US cents per kilowatt-hour, while consumers pay roughly 24 cents with the difference covered by subsidies. Recent moves include converting its Bel Air plant to LNG, expanding renewable capacity from about 56 MW in 2014 to approximately 624.8 MW in 2025, and announcing 104 oil and gas blocks for exploration. Energy and Petroleum Minister El Hadji Abdourahmane Diouf made the block announcement in October.
items.title: Senegal Targets Gas and Renewables to Cut Power Costs

items.summary: Inside Climate News reports that the Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection issued a new permit in May allowing companies to reclassify conventional oil and gas wells as mineral brine wells, enabling them to sell radioactive wastewater as a product and spread it on roads. David Hess, a former DEP secretary, called the rule ridiculous on its face. Charlie Palladino said roadspreading does not control dust effectively and can damage pavement. Academic research suggests wastewater controls dust no better than rainwater. Karen Feridun testified that over 3.5 million gallons of wastewater had been dumped between 2018 and 2024. DEP says a brine well permit will not necessarily allow roadspreading, but it is drafting regulations to clarify the process.
items.title: Pennsylvania Opens a New Loophole for Oil and Gas Wastewater Disposal

items.summary: In an interview with Living on Earth, pediatrician Dr. Leonardo Trasande discusses a study published in the journal Nature that found micro- and nanoplastics generate free radicals when exposed to water, challenging the assumption that plastic is chemically inert. Trasande explains that increased inflammation may underlie conditions such as cardiovascular disease, heart attack and stroke. He notes this research further unravels why microplastics were linked to a fourfold increase in those outcomes found earlier by the New England Journal of Medicine. The study focuses on one aspect of plastic’s threat while acknowledging chemicals remain a separate concern. Trasande suggests reducing exposure through glass, stainless steel and cast iron cookware rather than nonstick products. He frames environmental exposures as an emerging third risk factor alongside diet and physical activity. Inside Climate News reports the interview.
items.title: Pediatrician Says New Study Shows Microplastics Are Biologically Active

items.summary: Groww has opened direct investing in US stocks and ETFs to all customers, giving access to companies such as NVIDIA, Apple, Microsoft and Tesla. The platform offers more than 10,000 US-listed securities and supports fractional shares so investors can buy portions of a share instead of full units. Choosing between individual stocks and funds depends on an investor's risk appetite, horizon and objectives.
items.title: Groww Opens US Stock Investing to All Indian Customers

items.summary: The UK government’s upcoming budget briefly mentions a new focus on long-term outcomes, giving it one paragraph in the 166-page document. Preventative spending that pays for itself through future savings will be ringfenced from next year via preventative departmental expenditure limits (PDELs). Officials call it an important reform, but departments await Treasury guidance and uncertainty remains over what qualifies.
items.title: UK budget introduces world-first long-term spending protection

items.summary: Cryptocurrency exchange Binance said on Saturday it has covered 90 per cent of the amount stolen after a record $6.3 billion hack of its platform, Oct 31 reported. The remaining 10 per cent involves less liquid tokens that may take longer to source. Binance set aside around $6.34 billion internally and partially deployed its $1 billion Secure Asset Fund for Users (SAFU). Co-CEO Richard Teng called the breach a 'complex attack' involving a compromised laptop and malicious software. The exchange remains on track to resume withdrawals Sunday, November 1.
items.title: Binance Covers Most of Record Hack Losses

items.summary: An Environmental Defense Fund analysis found that the Trump administration provided support to nearly half of the nation's coal plants, helping them continue operating despite economic and regulatory pressures. The study examined 184 grid-connected operating coal plants and reported that 90 received administrative support through cash handouts, Clean Air Act exemptions from pollution limits, and requirements to stay online past their retirement dates. EDF attributed these measures to tools designed to extend plant lifespans while increasing electricity costs and pollution for Americans. NorthWestern Energy defended its Colstrip plant as state of the art technology, while NRG requested exemptions citing compliance costs. The administration stated it saved more than 100 coal plants this term.
items.title: EDF Report Finds Trump Administration Backed Half of US Coal Plants

items.summary: The author, who won the Elinor Ostrom Prize from the Institut Ostrom Catalunya, announced a talk in Barcelona scheduled for Wednesday, November 4 at 18:30 local time. Details were linked online, and they invited readers to attend.
items.title: Prize winner announces Barcelona talk on November 4

items.summary: A newly published paper in AEJ: Economic Policy by Carl Hase and Johannes Kasinger shows cannabis retailers in Washington state raised prices following organized retail crime. Matching store-level crime data to transaction records, the authors estimate a 1.7–1.8 percent price increase at victimized stores and nearby competitors, consistent with cost shocks rather than demand shifts. They estimate crime imposes about a 1 percent hidden unit tax, costing roughly $30.7 million in social costs borne by consumers.
items.title: Cannabis retailers raise prices after retail crime, study finds

items.summary: A massive fire at Hong Kong's Wang Fuk Court last year claimed 168 lives and exposed serious failures in building safety and government oversight, according to an independent committee report released this week. Residents had repeatedly raised concerns about fire hazards, but complaints were passed between authorities without proper action. The Independent Checking Unit relied on contractor certificates rather than checking risks itself. Findings point to misconduct by contractors and consultants alongside departmental failures. In response, the ICU will be disbanded and replaced by a new Public Housing Building Control Section; the housing secretary has resigned. Chief Executive John Lee's determination to hold those responsible accountable is praised as showing that official failures are not simply swept under the carpet.
items.title: Hong Kong draws lessons from Wang Fuk Court fire

items.summary: A CGTN commentator frames the Communist Party of China's Fifth Plenary Session of the 20th Central Committee, which closed in Beijing on October 29, around a question posed by Huang Yanpei in July 1945 about whether the Communists could escape dynastic cycles of rise and fall. The plenum adopted a resolution on persevering with full and rigorous Party self-governance, citing people's oversight over government and Party self-reform as two answers to avoiding that cycle. Drawing on anti-corruption figures from 2025 — including officials investigated and thousands given disciplinary punishments — the piece links these measures to the mass line and a party of roughly 101 million members organized in millions of grassroots organizations, while noting the problems remain unresolved. The author argues self-reform addresses pressures from markets and private capital without abolishing them, with resonance beyond China for ruling parties facing similar dangers.
items.title: CPC's Fifth Plenum Reaffirms Commitment to Party Self-Reform

items.summary: Hainan, an island province in southern China, has introduced a digital reporting system designed to reduce excessive and repetitive paperwork at the grassroots level. The system allows information to be submitted just once and shared across departments. By streamlining reporting, it aims to ease the administrative burden on local officials and free up more of their time to serve the public.
items.title: Hainan Launches Digital Reporting System for Grassroots Governance

items.summary: Government data show more than 5,000 deaths from an ongoing Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo. Eight of 26 provinces are affected, with over 10,300 confirmed cases and a case fatality rate of 48.6%. Public health officials say the epicentre remains Ituri province, a conflict zone that hampers containment. The World Health Organization says greater access to affected areas is needed to end it.
items.title: Congo's Ebola Outbreak Kills Over 5,000 in Deadliest Ever

items.summary: Profits at some of the UK's best-known charity shops have plummeted amid pressures including online secondhand platforms, prompting claims that a key part of the sector's fundraising model could be under threat. According to unpublished accounts seen by the Financial Times, Oxfam's retail profit fell 23% to £4.9m in the last financial year from £6.4m previously. The British Heart Foundation plans to close 150 stores after losses, while Cancer Research UK and Scope have also closed shops. Despite UK secondhand clothing spending quadrupling to £8.8bn a year per GlobalData, donated clothes are increasingly substandard. Robin Osterley of the Charity Retail Association attributed quality decline to fast fashion but disputed online platforms as an issue, citing budget pressures instead.
items.title: UK Charity Shops Face Profit Decline Amid Secondhand Market Shift

items.summary: Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed put his cabinet ministers and senior officials through military training at the Hurso centre, saying armed forces discipline could strengthen leadership. The move is unusual in Ethiopia, where civilian officials rarely undergo such training. Participants included Speaker Muferiat Kamil and Finance Minister Fitsum Assefa. It comes amid fighting in Tigray, Amhara and Oromia, plus tensions with Eritrea.
items.title: Ethiopian Prime Minister Sends Cabinet Ministers Through Military Training

items.summary: Reserve driver Ryo Hirakawa will replace Esteban Ocon at the US-owned Formula One team Haas for this weekend's Mexico City Grand Prix, the team said on Saturday. A spokesman said the change was not due to illness but gave no further details, and the governing FIA confirmed it. The 32-year-old Japanese Hirakawa takes part in his first practice Friday; the race will be his Formula One debut.
items.title: Hirakawa Replaces Ocon for Haas F1 Debut in Mexico City

items.summary: Residents and officials in Urda, Spain, gathered on Saturday (Oct 31) at the San Juan Bautista church near a high-speed train collision that killed at least 69 people. Investigators are examining one of Europe's deadliest rail disasters this century, which happened when a Madrid-to-Seville train struck a stationary train on Wednesday. Archbishop Francisco Cerro of Toledo called it
items.title: Spanish Village Holds Memorial Mass for Train Crash Victims

items.summary: Spain enters a third day of national mourning after a train collision in Urda, Toledo killed at least 69 people. Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez says the country is working tirelessly to identify victims while trust in Spain’s rail network has been further shaken. Authorities report 39 injured remain hospitalized and emergency services collected 31 bags of partial remains; authorities say 67 missing-person reports stay open, including 14 for foreign nationals. The crash occurred on a Madrid–Seville line also hit by a January collision that killed 46 people in Andalusia. Driver union Semaf demands urgent review of the failed LZB protection system and has called fresh strikes at Renfe; opposition leader Alberto Núñez Feijóo blames the government for not updating an obsolete safety system.
items.title: Spanish PM faces pressure after deadly Urda train crash

items.summary: EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas accused Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov of telling “a lot of lies” about the Ukraine war at G20 talks in Atlanta. British minister Ed Miliband also confronted him, urging Putin to accept Russia will not win. Lavrov dismissed Europe’s stance as an arrogant boycott and called Washington’s approach a lesson.
items.title: Kallas calls Lavrov a liar over Ukraine

items.summary: Turkey nominated former foreign minister and longtime UN ambassador Feridun Hadi Sinirlioglu for the next UN secretary-general, per state-media reports. President Recep Tayyip Erdogan backed the submission; he has pushed to reform the Security Council. The role would begin January 1, replacing Antonio Guterres after nearly a decade. Sinirlioglu may face opposition from Greece and Israel as seven other candidates compete.
items.title: Turkey Nominates Former Foreign Minister Sinirlioglu as UN Chief

items.summary: Residents evacuated from Russia-occupied Oleshky arrived in Ukraine under the most significant truce since Russia's invasion of Ukraine in 2022. The Kherson region ceasefire, which the White House says US first lady Melania Trump helped broker, began Tuesday at 3am and is expected to continue through Sunday evening. About 2,000 residents remained; one humanitarian convoy could safely evacuate more than 750 people. Families separated for over two years reunited at the border.
items.title: Oleshky Evacuees Reach Ukraine Amid Ceasefire

items.summary: Residents of Oleshky, a city in Ukraine's Kherson region under Russian occupation since 2022, crossed into Ukrainian-held territory Saturday after an evacuation operation routed through Belarus during a rare truce. The pause in fighting began Tuesday and is the longest along any part of the front line since Russia invaded in February 2022; it was brokered by US First Lady Melania Trump, who announced the ceasefire on October 23 (date-1024-1026) and credited her mediation. AFP met evacuees disembarking buses in northern Chernigiv region, where some embraced family members after months of starvation. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said residents would receive needed assistance and thanked the American side for its role (s13-s14). Around 2,000 residents remained before the operation, down from 24,000 pre-invasion (quantity-3088-3103, quantity-3119-3125), per Kyiv's estimates. The truce is scheduled to end Sunday evening (s29).
items.title: Oleshky Evacuees Reunite With Families After Truce-Brokered Rescue

items.summary: UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham said Saturday he was open to the UK issuing a formal apology for its role in the transatlantic slave trade but ruled out financial reparations. Writing in The Guardian ahead of King Charles III's Caribbean tour and Commonwealth summit, Burnham pledged difficult conversations while arguing British people today cannot be held liable for historical wrongs from a different age. Denis O'Brien of The Repair Campaign urged London to give a full apology now.
items.title: Burnham Open to Slavery Apology, Rejects Reparations

items.summary: Senegal is hosting the opening ceremony of the Youth Olympic Games on Saturday, marking the first time an Olympic event reaches Africa as the continent pursues a larger role in international sport. About 2,700 young athletes aged 14 to 17 will compete through Nov. 13 across Dakar, Diamniadio and Saly. The games were originally scheduled for 2022 but the coronavirus pandemic delayed them by four years. Athletes will contest 153 medal events across 25 sports, including several debuts such as Baseball5, Wushu and coastal rowing beach sprint. President Bassirou Diomaye Faye is set to declare the games open at 6:30 p. m.
items.title: Senegal Opens Youth Olympic Games in Dakar

items.summary: The second and final day of a G20 foreign ministers' meeting is underway Saturday, 31 October 2026, in the US city of Atlanta. Hosted by Secretary of State Marco Rubio, the two-day gathering opened with his remarks instead of a traditional group photo, following indications from several European officials that they would not pose alongside Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov amid tensions over the war in Ukraine.
items.title: G20 Foreign Ministers' Meeting Enters Final Day in Atlanta Amid Global Tensions

items.summary: Iran's Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei ordered his military chiefs to respond to any attack on Iran with an immediate, impactful and geographically unrestricted response. The orders suggest Tehran would broaden its targets beyond predominantly military ones, widen the war across the region if the US and Israel launch a new attack, update its Targets Bank of US and Israeli assets, and instruct Hezbollah and Hamas to engage. They come after four oil tankers hit mines in the Strait of Hormuz. Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Iran does not rule out war but welcomed diplomatic efforts, with Qatar mediating talks that shortened an implementation period from five days to two. Iran's Revolutionary Guard attributed the tanker explosions to unauthorised routes and ignored warnings; Oman evacuated 25 crew members off Musandam Governorate, 1. 6 nautical miles offshore." We do not rule out any possibility regarding the outbreak of war," Araghchi said."
items.title: Iran Orders Unrestrained Response to Any Attack

items.summary: The U.N. biodiversity conference (COP17) in Yerevan, Armenia, produced roughly $1.8 billion in new nature-finance announcements at the close of its session, including a $500 million commitment from the Netherlands to the Tropical Forest Forever Facility on Oct. 26 and another half-billion-dollar contribution from the Global Environment Facility reported that day. Overall biodiversity spending remains far short of the $200 billion per year target set in the Kunming-Montreal framework, with OECD data suggesting annual finance reached no more than $92 billion by 2025.
items.title: COP17 biodiversity conference delivers finance pledges amid shortfalls on spending and subsidies

items.summary: Two men wearing head torches entered the Fondazione Magnani Rocca museum near Parma on March 22, forcing a window and removing Cezanne, Renoir and Matisse works worth about €9 million ($10 million) within three minutes before handing them to an accomplice. A fourth man discharged a fire extinguisher at the gate when the alarm sounded. Director Stefano Roffi said “Whatever could go wrong, did.” The theft follows recent European museum break-ins.
items.title: European Museums Heighten Security After Parma Art Heist

items.summary: Raids on online scam centers in Madagascar revealed links to a criminal group that ran similar operations in Cambodia, allegedly defrauding African nationals through human trafficking. The sites conducted romance, cryptocurrency and investment fraud, mostly run by Chinese nationals, 148 of whom have been extradited to China, according to Madagascar's justice ministry. Thirteen compounds were dismantled in August and September with U.S. DOJ cooperation.
items.title: Madagascar Raids Expose Scam Centers Linked to Cambodia Network

items.summary: A South African court permitted the March and March movement to hold its planned demonstrations under amended conditions, restricting marches between 9am and 3pm and barring weapons or face coverings. Acting Police Minister Firoz Cachalia sought to block the events over public-order concerns amid unrest in Durban that police say has spread violence; counsel described it as lawlessness requiring more than 400 officers deployed. March and March defended its constitutional right to protest, distancing itself from any violence.
items.title: South African Court Imposes Conditions on Anti-Migrant Marches

items.summary: The Congress-led opposition unanimously passed a 'resolution' in a Saturday 'mock Parliament' at Mallikarjun Kharge's residence to remove Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls. Kharge accused him of centralising control and acting on behalf of PM Modi and Amit Shah, while Rahul Gandhi called it a political weapon. The article notes that real removal requires Supreme Court-judge-style grounds with heavy parliamentary majorities.
items.title: Congress bloc holds mock Parliament resolution against CEC Gyanesh Kumar amid electoral roll row

items.summary: The Indian government permitted exports of agarwood oil and chips through Lokpriya Gopinath Bordoloi International Airport in Guwahati, per a Directorate General of Foreign Trade notification published on October 31, 2026. Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal said the approval responds to Chief Minister Himanta Biswa's request and is a logistical boost for Assam and the Northeast. The exports remain subject to all statutory requirements.
items.title: Government permits agarwood oil and chip exports from Guwahati airport

items.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi accused opposition forces of trying to create instability by spreading lies and rumours, calling them obstructionists after a decade of electoral defeats. He urged citizens to stand together against what he termed 'Dimagi Naxalism,' the threat posed by such mental unrest. The remarks came during Rashtriya Ekta Diwas celebrations in New Delhi on Saturday.
items.title: Modi Accuses Opposition of Conspiring to Divide Nation

items.summary: The 57th GST Council meeting on October 8 approved a range of process reforms centered on seller registration, returns and refunds. The decisions will be implemented through administrative processes in phases beginning Sunday, November 1, 2026. Changes include simplified registration for small e-commerce sellers, user-friendly filing interfaces, automatic refund processing and greater flexibility on post-supply discounts while retaining safeguards around credit notes.
items.title: GST Council approves registration reforms effective November 1, 2026

items.summary: A 66-year-old woman from Sau Mau Ping lost around HK$2.7 million to scammers who claimed her bank account was linked to money laundering, the South China Morning Post reported. She transferred HK$2 million and later HK$700,000 into designated accounts before lodging a police complaint on Saturday. Authorities registered it as deception; no arrests were made.
items.title: Elderly Woman Loses Millions After Fake Bank Investigation Scam in Hong Kong

items.summary: The Rajasthan government approved an Anti-Corruption Bureau investigation against senior IAS officer Shikhar Agrawal over allegations that he misused his position to favour a resort company, causing financial losses to the state. His wife, IPS officer Prashakha Mathur, was also placed on Awaiting Posting Orders. The inquiry centers on 40 villas and cottages allegedly bought by the couple at resorts in Udaipur and Alwar for around ₹15 lakh each, below market value.
items.title: Rajasthan Approves ACB Probe into IAS Officer Over Villa Deals

items.summary: BJP spokesperson Sambit Patra mocked Congress leader Rahul Gandhi, calling him a 'mock Prime Minister for life' and dismissing opposition protests as pointless. BJP's Sudhanshu Trivedi cited the World Bank report showing India's extreme poverty rate fell to 2.6 per cent in 2023 from 27.1 per cent in 2011, with an estimated 496 million (49.60 crore) people lifted out of poverty.
items.title: BJP Tells Rahul Gandhi He Is a Mock PM for Life

items.summary: Congress MP Abhishek Manu Singhvi defended an opposition mock parliament held at Congress President Mallikarjun Kharge's residence, where bloc leaders passed an impeachment motion against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Rahul Gandhi led the move, alleging treason and voter deletion, while BJP dismissed it as theatrics.
items.title: Opposition Holds Mock Parliament Over Election Commission Chief; BJP Calls It Theatrics

items.summary: The INDIA bloc is holding a large protest at Ramlila Maidan on Sunday, November 1, opposing alleged electoral irregularities and the Special Intensive Revision of voter rolls. Organisers expect up to 10 lakh participants, while Delhi Police estimate around 50,000; the ground holds roughly 45,000-50,000 when empty but about 30,000-40,000 with seating and enclosures. The rally runs between 10 am and 5 pm amid extensive security.
items.title: INDIA bloc stages Delhi rally against CEC Gyanesh Kumar

items.summary: Climate policy experts say the upcoming IPCC session in October may resolve a two-year deadlock over when its seventh assessment report (AR7) should be published. Some countries want all reports ready before 2028 to feed the second Global Stocktake, while India and other developing nations argue that rushing would compromise quality and inclusivity. T. Jayaraman and Tejal Kanitkar, both climate policy experts who served on India's IPCC delegations, were interviewed by Frontline. They say reports should be released between May/June 2028 and late 2029 to allow adequate review time. The pair dispute claims that developing countries seek to withhold the report, calling such allegations baseless. They note other scientific sources will inform GST2 regardless of IPCC timing.
items.title: IPCC Nations Clash Over AR7 Report Timeline

items.summary: A veterinary and conservation team in West Kalimantan rescued 53 Bornean orangutans between August 1 and October 21, 2026 during joint fire-fighting operations. Komara says rising flames force apes to flee higher, making darting dangerous, while many arrive thin and injured. He adds that burned peatland habitats mean rehabilitated animals cannot be released where they were found.
items.title: Team rescues orangutans amid Kalimantan forest fires

items.summary: The Opposition INDIA bloc staged a symbolic “public impeachment” of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar at Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge’s residence, accusing him of conspiring to steal elections by ensuring the intentional deletion of 13 crore voters during the special intensive revision of electoral rolls. The mock parliamentary event called for his resignation and demanded revocation of the 2023 appointment Act. It followed nationwide protests triggered by a September 23 Indian Express investigation into objections raised by two Election Commissioners over roll revisions.
items.title: Opposition INDIA bloc stages symbolic impeachment of Chief Election Commissioner

items.summary: Union Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw announced on Saturday that Prime Minister Narendra Modi had cleared the north corridor of the bullet train project, which will connect Delhi with Agra, Kanpur, Lucknow, Ayodhya, Varanasi, Prayagraj, Patna and Siliguri before extending to Guwahati. Vaishnaw said passengers could travel from Delhi to Kanpur in 1 hour and 45 minutes, while the Delhi-Agra leg would take 59 minutes. The project is expected to be fully 'Make in India', built using Indian capabilities for its construction work including pillars and girders.
items.title: Modi Clears North Corridor of Bullet Train Project

items.summary: The Bihar education department issued an order on October 30, 2026, banning T-shirts and jeans for teaching and non-teaching staff across state-run schools. Director Vijay Kumar Pandey directed dignified formal attire during office hours and prohibited dancing, DJ setups, disco and vulgar events inside school premises. The notice cited widespread non-compliance with earlier circulars and compared the rule to dress codes at India’s Supreme Court and Patna high court.
items.title: Bihar Bars Casual Wear and DJ Events at Schools

items.summary: The Georgia Court of Appeals reversed a lower court, ruling on October 29, 2026 that software developer Jeff White never formed an enforceable partnership with RutterKey Solutions LLC owner Bruce Mortimer. White claimed he had been promised 30% of joint venture profits since December 2018 and relied partly on a 2022 letter describing a 70-30 profit split. The appeals court found essential terms remained unresolved, so the agreement was only an agreement to agree. It also dismissed White's claims for unpaid services, noting RKS paid him $171,000 to $252,000 annually from 2019 through 2023 and treated him as a W-2 employee, so intellectual property created in that scope belonged to the company. The court observed that recorded profit-sharing discussions may not create an enforceable partnership when fundamental business terms stay undecided.
items.title: Georgia Court Rejects Developer's Profit-Sharing Partnership Claim

items.summary: The Open Space Institute has purchased a four-acre property for $1.3 million from the Margaret M. Rumsey Trust, located between Buttermilk Falls State Park and Route 13 in Tompkins County. The organisation plans to transfer the land to New York State as an addition to the park. Situated at the foot of the gorge that gave the park its name, the site includes a former bed-and-breakfast built around 1825. OSI says it could support a redesigned gateway, reconfigured parking, improved traffic flow, staff housing, and a new trailhead for nearly 400,000 annual visitors. The property will remain closed to the public while OSI owns it before transfer.
items.title: Open Space Institute buys land near Buttermilk Falls State Park

items.summary: The Enforcement Directorate detained Samajwadi Party leader Azam Khan from outside Rampur jail as he came out on bail in an alleged PAN fraud case. The 78-year-old will be produced before a special court in Ghaziabad, where officials seek his remand under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act. The Allahabad High Court had suspended his sentence and granted bail Thursday.
items.title: ED Detains Azam Khan on Bail in PAN Fraud Case

items.summary: Business continued at Conrad Bengaluru on Saturday as police and technical teams investigated the fatal electrocution of two foreign guests in its swimming pool. A hotel representative said staff focused on supporting victims' families, while an Assistant Commissioner confirmed a joint investigation with BESCOM and BWSSB into the pool's pump, lighting and earthing systems. The incident has drawn criticism over safety compliance at luxury hotels nationwide.
items.title: Conrad Bengaluru Opens for Business Despite Fatal Pool Electrocution Probe

items.summary: Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu directed police to immediately apprehend the accused who attacked a Class 10 student with a saw inside her classroom at Zilla Parishad High School in Raptadu, Anantapur district. The victim sustained severe injuries and another girl was also hurt. Naidu spoke with officials, medical teams, and the family, assuring assistance while condemning the brutality.
items.title: Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister Orders Arrest After Classroom Attack on Student

items.summary: The author argues that India is facing an existential crisis at both personal and collective levels, urging society to conduct a 'life review' of its institutions. He traces the term to existentialist philosophy and links it to recent protests over government corruption, exam-paper leaks, and electoral-roll erasures. The piece cites data: Forbes India reports 284 billionaires with roughly $1 trillion in combined wealth for 2025; a World Bank mid-2025 update found extreme poverty fell below the global average at about 2.6%, aided by welfare schemes; yet a 2025 Review of Agrarian Studies study put population below the poverty line at 26.4%. The author blames 'trickle-down' economic policy and an eroded democracy since 2014, framing calls for change as essential to confronting the crisis.
items.title: India's Author Calls for a National Life Review Amid Existential Crisis

items.summary: S Naren, Chief Investment Officer of ICICI Prudential Mutual Fund, spoke at the ET Wealth Expo in Mumbai about why treating individual stocks like asset classes is riskier than diversifying across asset classes. He used 1990 Sensex composition to illustrate how few companies survive over time and argued that beaten-down stocks may never recover their former value. Naren identified NASDAQ and the US dollar as anti-asset allocation bets, noting the dollar moved from 80 to 157 against the yen, while still supporting a small gold allocation. He cautioned investors about chasing strong Indian midcap and smallcap returns since 2020, stressing that individual company performance does not make an entire segment attractive for asset allocation. As he said: 'Stocks need not mean revert at all.' The article carries a disclaimer that expert views are their own and do not represent the Economic Times' position.
items.title: ICICI Prudential's S Naren Warns Against Treating Stocks as Asset Classes

items.summary: Several mutual fund houses have temporarily halted fresh investments in gold fund-of-funds from mid-October, including new SIPs and switch-ins. Reasons are undisclosed but may relate to rising gold imports and strong inflows. Gold ETFs remain open for purchases without a demat account as an alternative.
items.title: Gold FoF Curbs Prompt Investors to Seek Alternatives

items.summary: Mumbai head coach Amol Muzumdar says the Indian women's cricket team can dominate world cricket consistently within two years, backed by young talent from age-group programs. India won its first ODI World Cup at home last November but has no major T20I title yet. Speaking at an event organised by the Sports Journalists Association of Mumbai (SJAM), Muzumdar and captain Smriti Mandhana will target that gap in the inaugural six-team ICC T20I Champions Trophy.
items.title: India's Women's Coach Sees Dominance Within Two Years

items.summary: A patient at a municipal hospital in Nalasopara West, Palghar district was allegedly assaulted around midnight by two men who entered the ward and attacked him while he lay on his bed. The victim, Kaleem Khan, had been admitted since October 28 after fever and low platelets. Hospital In-Charge Gaurav Wagh said an argument with his wife preceded it; a video has circulated online.
items.title: Hospital Patient Allegedly Beaten By Wife's Brothers In Nalasopara West

items.summary: A 33-year-old woman, Ekta Bhangde, and her six-year-old son Madhav died after falling from a high-rise housing complex in Pimpri-Chinchwad on Friday evening. Wakad police are investigating; bodies were sent for post-mortem. Police said it is likely suicide, noting CCTV showed the mother taking her son to the 18th floor by elevator and no note found.
items.title: Woman and Son Die in Pune High-Rise Fall

items.summary: A Delhi court issued a fresh bailable warrant against YouTuber Dhruv Rathee in an eight-year-old criminal defamation case filed by Vikas Pandey. The Saket court directed the warrant be served at his Gurugram address after learning he had left India and that earlier warrants failed—October 17's was sent to an incorrect Austrian address, while another could not be executed because premises were locked. Proceedings have faced repeated service difficulties since 2019; the next hearing is fixed for November 23.
items.title: Delhi Court Issues Fresh Bailable Warrant Against Dhruv Rathee
